results.name: Jump Rope Row
instructions: Loop the jump rope over a vertical bar or similar stable structure, ensuring the rope is at about hip height. Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles of the jump rope with both hands.
Step back slightly to create tension in the rope, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Pull the rope towards your torso by bending your elbows and bringing your hands towards your sides, engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles.
Extend your arms back out to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull the rope towards your torso to maximize muscle engagement.
Ensure the vertical bar or structure is stable and can support the tension in the rope to prevent slipping or injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the rope towards your torso and inhaling as you extend your arms back out.
results.description: Jump Rope Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Kettlebell Gorilla Row
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width apart, bend your knees, and hinge forward with a straight back. Grip a kettlebell in each hand between your feet.
Keep your left kettlebell on the floor and pull the right kettlebell toward your abdomen, driving your elbow back close to your body.
Lower the right kettlebell to the floor, then pull the left kettlebell toward your abdomen in the same way.
Continue alternating sides while keeping your torso and hips stable.
tips: Keep your back straight and your torso still.
Keep your elbow close to your body as you row.
Avoid twisting your torso as you lift the weight.
Exhale as you row and inhale as you lower the kettlebell.
results.description: Kettlebell Gorilla Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Kettlebell Pullover
instructions: Lie with your upper back supported on a flat bench, your knees bent, and your feet firmly on the floor. Lift your hips and hold a kettlebell with both hands above your chest, using a neutral grip.
Keep your arms slightly bent and slowly lower the kettlebell behind your head.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch through your mid-back while keeping your hips raised.
Pull the kettlebell back above your chest with control, then repeat.
tips: Keep your hips raised throughout the entire exercise.
Avoid arching your lower back as the kettlebell lowers.
Lower the kettlebell behind your head in a smooth, controlled arc.
Inhale as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you raise it.
results.description: Kettlebell Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Kettlebell Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees, and hinge forward with your back straight. Hold a kettlebell in each hand using a neutral grip and let your arms hang down.
Pull both kettlebells toward the sides of your abdomen, driving your elbows upward and backward close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your torso still.
Lower both kettlebells with control until your arms are extended, then repeat.
tips: Maintain the same torso position throughout each repetition.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you row.
Pull the kettlebells toward your abdomen rather than your shoulders.
Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
results.description: Kettlebell Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Row
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with your right foot forward and your left leg slightly back. Bend your knees slightly, lean forward, rest your right arm on your right thigh, and hold the kettlebell in your left hand with a neutral grip.
Let your left arm hang toward the floor with your palm facing inward.
Pull the kettlebell toward the left side of your abdomen, driving your elbow back close to your body.
Lower the kettlebell with control until your arm is extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Keep your working elbow close to your body as you pull.
Fully extend your arm at the bottom without rounding your back.
Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
results.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Kipping Pull Up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Start a rhythmic swing by pushing your chest through your arms, then pulling your legs forward.
At the front of the swing, drive your hips up and pull hard with your arms to bring your chin over the bar.
Push away from the bar as you descend and flow straight into the next swing.
tips: Learn strict pull-ups first; kipping puts more stress on the shoulders.
Keep your core tight to control the swing.
results.description: Kipping Pull Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Abdominals.

results.name: Land Mine Row
instructions: Straddle the landmine bar facing away from the anchor, or stand beside it, and hinge at your hips with a flat back.
Grip the bar just below the plates, with a V-handle or both hands.
Row the bar toward your chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar with control until your arms are straight and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat and your hips still throughout.
Pull toward your lower chest, not your neck.
results.description: Land Mine Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Lower Back.

results.name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar with both hands at hip height.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at your hips and push them back as you lower the bar along your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
tips: The movement is a hip hinge, not a squat.
Keep the bar close to your body.
results.description: Landmine Romanian Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Forearms.

results.name: Lat Pull Down Close Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands just closer than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Lat Pull Down Close Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Lat Pull Down Normal Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands, just wider than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Lat Pull Down Normal Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.
